policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'And when he saw that it pleased the Jews' renders the connective as 'And' either way: ASV uses 'And' for both δέ and καί, and the Greek word order (ἰδὼν δὲ vs Καὶ ἰδὼν) leaves no English trace. No note maps here.

The variant is the article αἱ before ἡμέραι. ASV 'And those were the days of unleavened bread' supplies its own determiner ('those ... the'), which English requires regardless; the Greek article is not distinguished.

ASV 'prayer was made earnestly of the church unto God' renders an adverb modifying the verb, matching ἐκτενῶς. The adjectival ἐκτενὴς would qualify προσευχή ('earnest prayer was made'), which ASV does not have.
ASV 'for him' translates περὶ αὐτοῦ and ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ alike; ASV renders both prepositions 'for' in prayer contexts. Nothing in the English or a note distinguishes them.

ASV 'was about to bring him forth' renders προάγω, whose sense is to lead out/forth; προσαγαγεῖν (bring before, present to) would not yield 'forth', so r01 is excluded. Aorist vs present infinitive and the position of αὐτὸν leave no English trace, so r00-base, r02 and r03 all stand.
ASV 'And the angel said unto him' renders δέ and τε alike as 'And'; the connective is not distinguished and no note maps here.
ASV 'Gird thyself' translates the simple and the compound imperative identically; ASV does not mark the περί- prefix separately elsewhere and no note maps here.
ASV 'And he went out, and followed' leaves the verb without an object. The RP addition αὐτῷ would be rendered 'followed him'; ASV prints no object, italicized or otherwise.
The variant is word order only (ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος vs γενόμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ). ASV 'And when Peter was come to himself' is the same English for both.

The variant is the presence of the Greek article. ASV's definite articles here ('the Lord', 'the hand', 'the people') are required by English idiom and do not report the Greek article's presence or absence.
The variant is the Greek article. ASV 'the mother of John' supplies the article English idiom requires; the presence or absence of τῆς is not distinguished.
ASV 'And when he knocked at the door of the gate' renders the pronoun αὐτοῦ. The RP reading τοῦ Πέτρου would give 'when Peter knocked'; ASV names Peter nowhere in the verse.
The variant is word order only (ἐστιν αὐτοῦ vs αὐτοῦ ἐστιν). ASV 'It is his angel' is the same English for both.
ASV 'But he, beckoning unto them with the hand' renders the connective adversatively; ASV uses 'But' for both τε and δέ at a turn in the narrative, so neither reading is distinguished.

The variant is the article before the place name. ASV 'from Judaea to Caesarea' uses no article with either proper noun, as English idiom requires, so τὴν is not distinguished. The mapped note is a Greek gloss on 'put to death' and does not bear on this unit.

ASV 'Now he was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon' has the pronoun as subject. The RP addition ὁ Ἡρῴδης would be rendered 'Herod was highly displeased'; ASV names Herod only in the preceding verse.

ASV renders the participial chain as coordinated finite verbs ('arrayed himself ... and sat ... and made an oration'), supplying 'and' at each link whether or not καί stands in the Greek. The mapped note is classed alternative_rendering (judgment-seat) and cannot decide a reading.
The variant is word order only (Θεοῦ φωνὴ vs Φωνὴ θεοῦ). ASV 'The voice of a god' is the same English for both.
The variant is the Greek article before δόξαν. ASV 'gave not God the glory' uses the article English idiom requires in this phrase; it does not report whether τὴν stood in the Greek.
ASV 'But the word of God grew and multiplied' renders θεοῦ. The WH reading κυρίου would give 'the word of the Lord', which ASV does not print here.

ASV text reads 'returned from Jerusalem', with a note classed textual_variant mapped here: 'Many ancient authorities read to Jerusalem.' The note puts εἰς in the margin, so the base reading r00-base is excluded from the text. Both ἐξ and ἀπὸ are rendered 'from' and are not distinguished from each other.
ASV 'taking with them John whose surname was Mark' has no adjunctive adverb. The RP addition καί before Ἰωάννην would be rendered 'taking with them also John'; ASV prints no 'also'.
